The preview would write: --post stops being the sign-off on what was shown and the run without it becomes an unattended public post — the unrecoverable half of hazard one. Caught by the preview test's toHaveLength(1) on the gh calls.

The class claim the lane exists for, hollowed out: one comment posted, the first thread resolved, the rest left open while the timeline reads as if the class was disposed — worse than no tool, because it lies about coverage. Caught by the one-resolve-per-member count.

The mechanism without the membership: a reader of any one resolved thread can no longer see which class it was disposed with, and a reader of the comment cannot see what was resolved — the disposition stops being auditable, which is what makes class disposal acceptable at all.

A resolve that did not come back is the write half of the failure the exit code exists for: exit 0 on a half-disposed class tells the operator to move on, exactly the 'looks handled' failure one level up. The CLI test asserts the 1 and the named id.

A comment that failed to post must fail the command rather than reporting success: exiting 0 when the comment failed leaves the reviewer's finding marked handled on GitHub without the explanation on the timeline. Caught by the CLI test asserting exit code 1 when commentUrl is null.

Ignoring GraphQL errors on the write mutation produces silent false-success: the mutation fails on the server while the tool reports the class disposed. Caught by the mutation error test asserting a refusal.

Consuming the next flag as a value (e.g. --pr --thread or --thread --body) quietly accepts malformed invocations and corrupts parsed arguments rather than halting with a missing-value error. Caught by the argument test asserting missing value for flag.

Truncating thread retrieval at page one silently excludes threads past the 100-thread boundary, falsely reporting open threads as nonexistent. Caught by the multi-page fetch test asserting threads on subsequent pages are accumulated and recognized.

Reporting success before verifying every thread resolved presents a partial failure as a whole success: the operator sees 'class disposed' on stdout while the thread remains open. Caught by the CLI test asserting that 'class disposed' is not logged when a thread fails to resolve.
